item.title: Nintendo Switch 2 Tethered Jailbreak Uses OpenAI Codex and SmileBASIC 4
item.description:
Nintendo Switch 2 Tethered Jailbreak Uses OpenAI Codex and SmileBASIC 4

A Nintendo Switch 2 console has been jailbroken, and a modder demonstrated a custom Mario Kart World with new playable characters using a software‑only, tethered exploit that leverages an older game and OpenAI’s Codex.

🔍 Overview

  • The Switch 2 jailbreak is software‑only and tethered, meaning it must be launched from a game each time the console powers on.
  • A modder ran a custom version of Mario Kart World featuring Cinnamoroll, the red Angry Bird, Peter Griffin, and Steve from Minecraft.
  • The exploit was created with the assistance of OpenAI’s Codex, referred to as the “ns2jb” jailbreak.
  • The exploit is built around the game SmileBASIC 4, which lets users program and play games (though another modder says the title is “not strictly needed”).

🧩 How it Works

  • An older game (SmileBASIC 4) is used as the launch point for the jailbreak.
  • OpenAI Codex contributed code that enables the “ns2jb” jailbreak.
  • Because the jailbreak is tethered, the user must run it from the game every time the console is turned on.
  • The method does not modify hardware; it operates entirely in software.

🎮 Custom Content

Character Source
Cinnamoroll Sanrio
Red Angry Bird Angry Birds
Peter Griffin Family Guy
Steve Minecraft

⚙️ Key Details

  • Software‑only: No hardware changes are required.
  • Tethered: Must be executed from a game on each boot.
  • Required game: SmileBASIC 4 (though its necessity is disputed by another modder).
  • AI involvement: OpenAI’s Codex was used to develop the jailbreak code.

#NintendoSwitch2 #jailbreak #OpenAI #Codex

Source: Someone hacked the Switch 2 by using an old game and AI

item.title: Python Web UI for Mobile File Editing Built with Codex Remote and GPT-6
item.description:
Python Web UI for Mobile File Editing Built with Codex Remote and GPT-6

I built a Python web app on my phone using Codex Remote and GPT-6 Astra Extra High to view and edit files in a folder without routing credentials through the LLM.

🔍 Overview

  • Project created on 12th October 2026 from a phone.
  • Goal: edit a credentials file directly, avoiding round‑tripping through the LLM.
  • Result: a web UI for browsing and editing files in a folder.

🛠️ How it works

  • Codex Remote and GPT‑6 Astra Extra High generated the Python web app.
  • The app runs over a Tailscale network, allowing an agent to start it and a phone to connect securely.
  • File browsing interface is provided (see image).
  • Editing is powered by CodeMirror 6.
  • Monaco was considered but was rejected because it lacks a great mobile experience.

⚙️ Key details

  • Uses Python 3.11 (as indicated by the “Hello Python 3.15, goodbye 3.10, and now I can use 3.11” note).
  • Designed for mobile use: accessible from a phone via Tailscale.
  • Credentials remain on the device; they are not sent through the LLM.

🚀 Availability

  • Intended to be launched by an agent on the Tailscale network.
  • Once running, files can be edited directly from the phone’s browser.

#Python #Codex #GPT6 #Tailscale #WebUI

Source: Release: web-edit 0.1a0

item.title: Codex Pooler Introduced as Self-Hosted Gateway for Codex-Compatible Agents
item.description:
Codex Pooler Introduced as Self-Hosted Gateway for Codex-Compatible Agents

Codex Pooler is a self-hosted gateway designed to run Codex-compatible agents, tools, and automation using stable Pool API keys.

🔍 Overview

Codex Pooler allows operators to manage pools, accounts, API keys, saved resets, routing, request accounting, audit logs, and health. The system is designed so that operators do not store raw Codex secrets, bearer tokens, prompts, files, audio, or images.

🧩 How it works

Clients send OpenAI-compatible or Codex backend requests to the Codex Pooler. The system then selects an eligible account based on the following criteria:

  • Model support
  • Quota evidence
  • Limits
  • Session continuity
  • Routing policy
  • Health

⚙️ Key details

Feature Description
Stable Pool API keys Provides clients with one credential regardless of whether the Pool has one or several upstream accounts, avoiding the distribution of raw Codex account material.
Eligibility-aware routing Routes requests to accounts with matching health, session state, Pool policy, usable quota evidence, and compatible model support.
Codex backend compatibility Allows Codex-compatible clients to point at Codex Pooler while maintaining usage, compacting, and responses.

💡 Why it matters

  • Credential Isolation: It works with one upstream Codex account for client normalization, metadata-only operations, saved reset visibility, and credential isolation.
  • Scalability: Additional accounts can be added for routing and shared capacity across eligible accounts.
  • Stability: The Pool key remains stable even when capacity, reset policy, lifecycle state, and upstream assignments change.
  • Administrative Control: Instance owners maintain the global administration surface, while instance admins are restricted to their assigned Pools.

#Codex #API #AIagents #SelfHosted

Source: icoretech/codex-pooler

item.title: Ruflo Launches as an Agent Meta-Harness for Claude Code and Codex
item.description:
Ruflo Launches as an Agent Meta-Harness for Claude Code and Codex

Claude Flow has been renamed to Ruflo, an agent meta-harness and execution layer designed for Claude Code and Codex.

🔍 Overview

Ruflo serves as the execution layer around Claude Code and Codex, providing a system that allows for the deployment of intelligent multi-player swarms and the coordination of autonomous workflows. It integrates with native Claude Code, Codex, and Hermes, among others.

⚙️ Key details

Ruflo provides several technical capabilities to enhance agent operations:

  • Memory and Learning: Features adaptive memory, self-learning intelligence, and the ability to remember across sessions.
  • Coordination: Supports coordinated swarms and the ability for agents to self-organize.
  • Connectivity: Includes federation for secure communication across machines without leaking data and vector RAG integration.
  • Security: Includes enterprise security guardrails.
  • Scale: Adds over 100 specialized agents.

🧩 How it works

Users can set up the system with the command npx ruflo init. Once initialized, the system functions as follows:

  • Integration: Users continue to use Claude Code normally.
  • Automation: A hooks system automatically routes tasks and coordinates agents in the background.
  • Optimization: The system learns from successful patterns and every task.
  • Simplification: It removes the need to learn 26 CLI commands or 314 MCP tools.

#Ruflo #ClaudeCode #AIagents #Codex

Source: ruvnet/ruflo

item.title: Claude Flow Rebrands as Ruflo Agent Meta-Harness
item.description:
Claude Flow Rebrands as Ruflo Agent Meta-Harness

Claude Flow has been renamed to Ruflo, an agent meta-harness designed for Claude Code and Codex. It serves as the execution layer that provides models with tools, memory, loops, sandboxes, and controls to enable autonomous workflows.

🔍 Overview

Ruflo acts as a “nervous system” for Claude Code, allowing agents to self-organize into swarms and collaborate. Users can initialize the system with npx ruflo init, after which the hooks system automatically routes tasks and coordinates agents in the background without requiring the user to learn 314 MCP tools or 26 CLI commands.

🧩 How it works

Ruflo operates on the principle that an Agent = Model + Harness. While the model handles the writing, the Ruflo harness provides the following:

  • Coordination: Deploys intelligent multi-player swarms and autonomous workflows.
  • Memory: Features adaptive, self-learning memory that remembers across sessions.
  • Federation: Enables secure communication between agents on different machines without leaking data.
  • Integration: Native support for Claude Code, Codex, Hermes, and vector RAG integration.
  • Security: Includes enterprise security guardrails.

⚙️ Key details

Ruflo is released under the MIT License and provides a 14-chapter guide covering topics from initial tasks and memory to agent teams, plugins, cost, and verification.

item.title: GPT-6 Astra Integration with Blender for 3D Model Generation
item.description:
GPT-6 Astra Integration with Blender for 3D Model Generation

A user has demonstrated the ability to generate 3D .blend files by combining ChatGPT Images 2.5 and GPT-6 Astra running in Codex.

⚙️ Key details

  • Workflow: An image of a Faberge egg themed after the TV show Pluribus was generated using ChatGPT Images 2.5, then pasted into Codex running GPT-6 Astra (high).
  • Process: The user prompted the system to “Use your blender local skill to create a blender model of this faverge egg”.
  • Performance: The system processed the request for 17m51s to build several .blend files.

item.title: Analysis of the OpenAI Codex desktop application runtime components
item.description:
Analysis of the OpenAI Codex desktop application runtime components

The OpenAI Codex desktop application, which has been rebranded to ChatGPT, includes a large runtime environment containing a variety of bundled software dependencies.

⚙️ Key details

The application maintains a 1.7GB folder titled codex-primary-runtime. This directory includes the following software components:

Component Description
Python Full installation
Node.js Full installation
Poppler Native binary
git Native binary
LibreOffice Open source office suite (forked from OpenOffice.org in 2010)

🧩 How it works

The application utilizes specific plugin scripts to interface with these bundled tools. The directory ~/.cache/codex-runtimes/codex-primary-runtime/plugins/openai-primary-runtime/plugins/documents contains skills that instruct the system on how to locate and execute these binaries.

#OpenAI #Codex #ChatGPT #SoftwareArchitecture

Source: Codex bundles LibreOffice
